Rashi on Zevachim 12a:16:1.english: Shall we say Rabbi Yochanan holds, etc.: From the fact that we needed to answer according to him concerning one who designates an offering after midday, it indicates that if one had not heard from him that living animals are permanently disqualified, it would be fitting to designate them forever. For perhaps disqualification applies only to slaughtered animals, as in the case of the scapegoat whose blood is poured out, as discussed in Tractate Yoma (62b).

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:12:1.hebrew: לאחר הקטרת אימורין כתיב - וליכא למידרשיה לעיכובא דעצמו, שלא הוקטרו אימוריו כשר, והאי הוא דרשינן למילתא אחריתי:
Rashi on Zevachim 12b:12:1.english: It is written after the burning of the sacrificial portions - And it is impossible to expound it as indispensable for itself (the offering), since if its sacrificial portions were not burned it is [still] valid; and this [verse] we expound for another matter.

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:14:1.hebrew: תרי הוא כתיבי - ואם אין השני ענין לאחר הקטרה, דהא כתיב חד, תנהו ענין לעבודת דם ולפסול בשלא לשמן. חד הוא כתיב באיל עולה של מילואים, בואתה תצוה, וחד הוא כתיב בויקרא גבי עולת בן צאן:
Rashi on Zevachim 12b:14:1.english: “It” is written twice - And if the second one is not needed for [the matter of] after the burning, since one is already written, apply it to the matter of the blood service and to invalidate [the offering] when it is not offered for its own sake. One “it” is written regarding the ram of the burnt offering of the inauguration, in [the section beginning] “And you shall command” (Exodus 29), and one “it” is written in Leviticus, regarding the burnt offering of the sheep:

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:14:2.hebrew: אשם נמי תרי (אשם) הוא כתיבי - חד בצו את אהרן, אחר הקטרה, וחד בויקרא — אשם הוא, אשם לה'. ואע"ג דליכא חד מינייהו דכתיב גבי עבודת דם, תן האחד באם אינו ענין לכך, כדאמרת בעולה:
Rashi on Zevachim 12b:14:2.english: A guilt offering, too, "it" is written twice - One in "Command Aaron" (Leviticus 6), after the burning of the portions, and one in Leviticus (7:5): "It is a guilt offering, a guilt offering to the Lord." And even though neither of them is written with regard to the blood service, [we say that] when one is placed in the other it is not needed for its own matter, and therefore [it is applied] to this [the blood service], as you said regarding the burnt offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:1:1.hebrew: יש דחוי בדמים - יש תורת דחוי בקדושת דמים, אע"פ שאינה קדושת הגוף, כגון הכא שהקדיש חציה, לא קדשה אלא לדמיה, שהרי אין לו חלק [אלא] בחציה, ואין קדושה ראויה לפשוט בכולה על פיו. ואפי' הכי שייך בה דחוי ותדחה עולמית, ולא אמרי' לא אלימא קדושת דמים ליפסל משום דחוי: לישנא אחרינא - יש דחוי בשביל הדמים שלא פרע לקנות חציה של חבירו, שלא היתה קנויה לו כשהקדישה, שעדיין לא קנה חציה משל חבירו. ואינ"ו נרא"ה למור"י:
Rashi on Zevachim 12b:1:1.english: There is disqualification in [a case of sanctity of] monetary value - There is the law of permanent disqualification even in sanctity of [monetary] value, although it is not sanctity of the body [of the animal]. For example, here, where he consecrated half of it, it was consecrated only for its value, since he has a share only in half of it, and it is not fitting for the sanctity to spread through all of it on his word. And even so, disqualification applies to it, and it is disqualified forever; and we do not say that the sanctity of monetary value is too weak to be disqualified because of permanent disqualification. Another explanation: There is disqualification because of the money, since he did not pay to acquire the half belonging to his fellow, which was not acquired by him when he consecrated it, as he had not yet acquired his fellow's half. And this does not seem [correct] to my teacher.

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:2:1.hebrew: והמיר דת - נדחה מקרבן. בהכל שוחטין (חולין דף ה:): "מעם הארץ" — פרט למומר:
Rashi on Zevachim 12b:2:1.english: And he apostatized - He was disqualified from [bringing] an offering. [As derived] in the chapter "Hakol Shochatin" (Chullin 5b): "From the people of the land" — this excludes an apostate.

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:3:1.hebrew: ונשתטה - נדחה, דבעינן דעת, במסכת ערכין בפ' האומר משקלי עלי (ערכין דף כא.):
Rashi on Zevachim 12b:3:1.english: And he became an imbecile - [The offering] is [thereby] disqualified, because knowledge [i.e., halakhic competence] is required, [as stated] in tractate Arakhin, in the chapter "One who says: My weight is upon me" (Arakhin 21a).

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:3:2.hebrew: נשתפה - שקט משעמומו, כגון "על הר נשפה" (ישעיהו יג), דמתרגם "על טורא שלויא":
Rashi on Zevachim 12b:3:2.english: Became sound of mind (nishtafa) - He grew calm from his stupor, like "upon a bare (nishpeh) mountain" (Isaiah 13), which [Targum] translates as "upon a tranquil (shelvya) mountain."

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:6:1.hebrew: הורו ב"ד שחלב מותר - נדחה לו, דאילו עבר השתא לאו בר קרבן הוא, דאמרינן בהוריות (דף ב:): יחיד שעשה בהוראת ב"ד פטור:
Rashi on Zevachim 12b:6:1.english: The court ruled that fat is permitted - It is [thereby] rejected for him, for if he were to transgress now [after the ruling], he would not be liable for an offering, as we say in [tractate] Horayot (page 2b): An individual who acted on the ruling of a court is exempt.

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:7:1.english: With this he began - and he expounds with it that [the offering] is rejected.

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:7:2.hebrew: התם - גבי מומר ושוטה, גברא אידחי מקרבן, קרבן לא אידחי. דכתיב "תורת חטאת זאת" — לא נדחת מישראל מן הכשרין. אבל הכא, תורת קרבן זה נדחית מן הכל:
Rashi on Zevachim 12b:7:2.english: There - Regarding the apostate and the imbecile, the person is disqualified from [bringing] an offering, [but] the offering itself is not disqualified. As it is written: "This is the law of the sin-offering" — [the offering] is not rejected from [the category of] the fit ones of Israel. But here, the law of this offering is rejected from everyone.

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:8:1.hebrew: למה לי למיתני זקן - ליתני זקנים:
Rashi on Zevachim 12b:8:1.english: Why do I need to teach "zaken" [in the singular] - Let it teach "zekenim" [in the plural]:

Rashi on Zevachim 12b:8:2.hebrew: בחדא - בישיבה אחת היו יושבין, וכולן היו כאיש אחד:
Rashi on Zevachim 12b:8:2.english: In one - They were sitting in one session, and all of them were like one person.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 12b:2.english: One who cast off the yoke of Torah and became accustomed to transgression. In another place (see Chullin 5a) it is derived from an inference in the verses (or, in the Rambam's language, 'from oral tradition') that an apostate cannot bring an offering, because 'the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination' (see Sefer HaMitzvot). And there they distinguish between one who is an apostate to the entire Torah (including an apostate to idolatry or one who publicly desecrates Shabbat) and one who is accustomed to other transgressions: if he became accustomed and was publicly known for a specific transgression, an offering is not accepted from him specifically for that transgression.

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Zevachim 12b:2.english: One who cast off the yoke of Torah and became accustomed to transgression. In another place (see Chullin 5a) it is derived from an inference in the verses (or, in the Rambam's language, 'from oral tradition') that an apostate cannot bring an offering, because 'the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination' (see Sefer HaMitzvot). And there they distinguish between one who is an apostate to the entire Torah (including an apostate to idolatry or one who publicly desecrates Shabbat) and one who is accustomed to other transgressions: if he became accustomed and was publicly known for a specific transgression, an offering is not accepted from him specifically for that transgression.

Tosafot on Zevachim 12b:16:1.hebrew: בן עזאי בק"ו מייתי לה - אף ע"ג דפסול שלא לשמן מוציאו מידי פגול דבעינן שיהיו כל מתירים בכשרות, לא דמיא להא דאמר בפ"ק דפסחים (דף יא): כל דין שתחילתו להחמיר וסופו להקל אינו דין. תימה: ובן עזאי, אי דריש אותה לשמה כשרה שלא לשמה פסולה, הא שאר קדשים כו' — קל וחומר מאי אהני ליה? ואי לא דריש, א"כ אשם ליעכב מהיקישא דכחטאת וכאשם:
Tosafot on Zevachim 12b:16:1.english: Ben Azzai derives it by an a fortiori inference - Even though [an offering slaughtered] not for its own sake [being] disqualified removes it from the status of piggul, since we require that all the permitting acts be in a valid state, this is not comparable to what is stated in the first chapter of Pesachim (11a): "Any argument whose beginning is to be stringent and whose end is to be lenient is not a valid argument." It is puzzling: And as for Ben Azzai, if he expounds that [the verse teaches that] if it was slaughtered for its own sake it is valid, [and] not for its own sake it is disqualified — but with regard to other offerings, etc. — what does the a fortiori inference accomplish for him? And if he does not expound it [that way], then [why not say that] a guilt offering should be prevented [from being valid when slaughtered not for its sake] from the analogy, "like the sin offering, so the guilt offering"?

Tosafot on Zevachim 12b:1:1.hebrew: וש"מ דחוי מעיקרו הוי דחוי - תימה, דגבי הדס אמרינן פ' לולב הגזול (סוכה דף לג:): היכא (דאשכחן) דאשחור מערב יו"ט דדחוי מעיקרא לא הוי דחוי? וי"ל, דשאני התם דבידו לתקנו. תדע, דגבי לולב שנקטם ראשו [מעי"ט] ועלתה בו תמרה [בי"ט] מיבעיא ליה אי יש דחוי אי לאו [ולא] פשטינן לה מהא, משום דנקטם אין בידו לתקנו. וא"ת, מ"ט דר' יוחנן דאמר דחוי מעיקרו הוי דחוי? לילף ממחוסר זמן דלא הוי דחוי, כדאמר בפ' שני שעירי (יומא דף סד.)? וי"ל, דשאני מחוסר זמן דחוזר [ונראה] ממילא. וא"ת, אמאי איצטריך לרבי יוחנן מיעוטא דמום בם? הני הוא דכי עבר מומם ירצו, הא כל הדחויים אם עבר מומם לא ירצו, הואיל ונידחו אידחו. הא מום עובר לא ילפינן [דלדחי] דלא הוי דחוי, דהתם ממילא הוי? וי"ל, דאיכא מום דאינו עובר אלא על ידי רפואה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 12b:1:1.english: And [we learn] from this that something disqualified from the outset is considered disqualified - This is difficult, for regarding the myrtle we say in the chapter "Lulav HaGazul" (Sukkah 33b): Where do we find that [a myrtle] turned black on the eve of the Festival, [and] something disqualified from the outset is not considered disqualified? And one can answer: There it is different, because it is in one's power to fix it. Know [that this is so], for regarding a lulav whose top was cut off, and a date-cluster grew in it [on the Festival], he was uncertain whether there is [the law of] disqualification or not, and we did not resolve it from this [case], because once it was cut off, it is not in one's power to fix it. And if you ask: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yochanan, who said that something disqualified from the outset is considered disqualified? Let us learn from [an animal] lacking the required time, which is not considered disqualified, as stated in the chapter "Shnei Se'irei" (Yoma 64a)? And one can answer: [An animal] lacking the required time is different, because it returns and becomes fit on its own. And if you ask: Why did Rabbi Yochanan need the limiting phrase "for they have a blemish in them"? That [verse] is [stating] only that when their blemish has passed, they are accepted; but [for] all disqualified [animals], if their blemish passed, they are not accepted, since they were [once] rejected, they remain rejected. [Now,] we do not derive from a passing blemish that it is not considered disqualified, since there it happens on its own? And one can answer: There is a blemish that does not pass except through medical treatment.

Tosafot on Zevachim 12b:21:1.hebrew: מה להצד השוה שבהן שכן יש בהן צד כרת - תימה: ולר"א דפסל חטאת ואשם, ליפסול נמי עולה, ותיתי מחטאת ואשם [ופסח]. וי"ל דשייך קצת צד כרת באשם, משום דאיכא אשם תלוי; ומיהו לא שייך כמו בחטאת ופסח, כדמוכח לעיל:
Tosafot on Zevachim 12b:21:1.english: "What about their common element? For they have an element of karet" - This is puzzling: According to Rabbi Eliezer, who disqualifies a sin offering and a guilt offering [offered for the sake of a different offering], let a burnt offering also be disqualified, and let it be derived from the sin offering, the guilt offering, [and the Paschal offering]. And one can answer that an element of karet is somewhat applicable to a guilt offering, because there is a suspensive guilt offering (asham taluy); but nevertheless it is not applicable as it is with a sin offering and a Paschal offering, as is proven above:

Tosafot on Zevachim 12b:7:1.hebrew: הכא קרבן אידחי - וגרע מדאידחי גברא. והא דמשמע איפכא בהוריות פ' בתרא (דף יא.) גבי נשיאות מהו שתפסיק, לא דמי; דהתם לא אידחי קרבן מן החלב שאכל, דעדיין הוא חייב קרבן. ור"ת פירש איפכא, דגבי הורו ב"ד לא היה דחוי דגברא אידחי, שאינו יודע אם פטור אם לאו; קרבן לא אידחי, דאי לא דהתירו ב"ד היה קרב, ונמצא שלא היה דחוי אלא ע"י טעותו. אבל הכא אפילו קרבן נמי אידחי, דכיון שהוא שוטה או מומר פטור הוא לכולי עלמא:
Tosafot on Zevachim 12b:7:1.english: Here the offering was also disqualified - And this is worse than [a case where] the person was disqualified. And as for the fact that the opposite is implied in Horayot, the last chapter (11a), regarding [the question of] whether the office of Nasi interrupts [the obligation] — it is not comparable; for there the offering was not disqualified from the fat that he ate, since he is still obligated to bring an offering. But Rabbeinu Tam explained the opposite: that in the case of "the court ruled," it was not [a case of] disqualification, for the person was disqualified, [in that] he does not know whether he is exempt or not; [but] the offering was not disqualified, for if the court had not permitted [it], it would have been offered, and it turns out that it was disqualified only through his error. But here, even the offering was also disqualified, since he is an imbecile or an apostate, [and] he is exempt according to everyone.

Zevachim 12a:16.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Abbahu: Shall we say that Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that consecrated animals are disqualified and are no longer fit for sacrifice after they have been disqualified once?
